text: I'll start by looking at the workspace layout and finding the discount code logic.
The discount logic is likely in `discounts.py`.

The root cause is clear: `_used_codes` is a module-level global set that records every applied code and never clears it, so a reusable code is blocked after its first use. Restarting the service clears the set, which matches the report. Let me check the tests to see what behavior is expected before changing it.
The test confirms discounts are reusable. I'll remove the global "used" tracking: the eligibility check no longer blocks reuse, and `apply_discount` no longer records codes.

args.summary: Root cause: library/discounts.py kept a module-level `_used_codes` set. Every time `apply_discount` applied a code, it added the code to that set, and `is_eligible` rejected any code already in the set. So a reusable code like SAVE10 worked once per process, and only started working again after a restart cleared the set. Fix: removed the `_used_codes` global, the bookkeeping in `apply_discount`, and the used-code check in `is_eligible`. Eligibility is now based only on the subtotal meeting `min_subtotal`, which matches the existing test `test_discount_object_is_reusable_across_separate_orders`. The full test suite passes (29 tests).
